title: fix(security): compile the signing-policy bypass out and describe the gate honestly
body:
## Summary

- **Bypass variable compiled out.** `DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` no longer exists in normal builds. It is behind a non-default, test-only cargo feature that cannot be compiled into a release profile.
- **Honest docs.** The did-git-sign docs now describe the parent-process gate as what it is: a guard against accidental and naive use, not a boundary against code running as the user.
- **Namespace restriction.** `-Y sign` now refuses every sshsig namespace except `git`.
- **Testable gate.** The decision is a pure function, so its rules are tested without mutating the process environment.

## Changes

### Policy bypass (`crates/did-git-sign`)

- **New feature.** `Cargo.toml` adds a non-default feature, `insecure-policy-bypass = []`.
- **`policy.rs`:**
  - `compile_error!` when `insecure-policy-bypass` is enabled without `debug_assertions`.
  - The `BYPASS_ENV` constant exists only with the feature.
  - `bypass_requested()` is a constant `false` without the feature. With the feature, it reads the variable and prints a warning on stderr whenever the bypass is used.
  - `AuditEntry.bypass` is kept so the audit log format is unchanged. Only a feature build can set it.
- **`sign.rs`:** the refusal message no longer tells callers how to override the policy.
- **Usage check.** `grep -r DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` across local clones of this repo, openvtc, verifiable-trust-infrastructure and cierge found no users outside this crate. openvtc's only historical reference was the vendored copy of did-git-sign it removed in #159.

### Security model documentation

- **`policy.rs` module doc**, rewritten:
  - **What the gate does:** refuses unless git or `ssh-keygen` is the parent, and records every attempt.
  - **What it cannot do:** code running as the user can run real git with did-git-sign as its signing program, read the VTA credential from the keyring, or edit the audit log.
  - **What protects the key:** the VTA credential in the OS keyring.
- **`README.md`:** the "Security Model" section gains "What protects the signing key" and "The signing gate is an accident guard, not a boundary". It also states that the release binary has no bypass switch. The existing bullets move under "Other properties".

### Gate changes

- **`sign.rs` `check_namespace`:** `handle_sign` refuses any namespace other than `vgi_core::GIT_SSHSIG_NAMESPACE` (`git`). The check runs before the buffer is read or the VTA is contacted. git signs commits, tags and push certificates in `git`, so git is unaffected. The code labels this as friction, not a boundary.
- **`policy.rs` `decide(bypass, parent) -> bool`:** a pure function of the bypass flag and the raw parent name (first word, lowercased, matched by `parent_is_allowed`). `evaluate` now just gathers the inputs and calls it.

### Tests and CI

- **`policy` unit tests:**
  - `decide` admits `git`, `Git.EXE`, `git-remote-https`, `ssh-keygen`, `git --no-pager`;
  - `decide` refuses `cargo`, `gitleaks`, empty, whitespace and unknown parents;
  - only a bypass admits an unknown parent;
  - a normal build never requests a bypass;
  - the existing env-bypass test is gated on the feature and `#[serial]`.
- **`sign` unit tests:**
  - only `git` passes `check_namespace` (`file`, `email`, `""`, `Git`, `"git "`, `"git\0"` are refused);
  - `handle_sign` with namespace `file` and nonexistent paths fails with the namespace error, which shows nothing was read first.
- **`tests/policy_bypass.rs`** (new, `serial_test`):
  - a normal build with the variable set to `1`/`true`/`TRUE` still refuses a non-git parent and records `bypass: false`;
  - a feature build honours the variable and records it;
  - the default gate refuses a non-git parent.

  These tests assume the test process's parent is not git, which holds under cargo and nextest.
- **`ci.yml` `test` job**, two new steps:
  - `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass`;
  - `cargo build --release --locked -p did-git-sign`, failing if `target/release/did-git-sign` contains the string `DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY`.

## Verification (local, rustc/cargo 1.98.1, macOS)

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo clippy -p did-git-sign --all-targets --features insecure-policy-bypass -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo test --workspace` | exit 0, 144 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` (debug) | exit 0, 73 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo build --release --locked -p did-git-sign` | exit 0; `grep -a -c DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` on the binary: 0 |
| `cargo build -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` (debug) | exit 0; the same grep on the binary: 1, so the CI check detects the name when it is present |
| `cargo build --release -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` | exit 101: `error: the did-git-sign 'insecure-policy-bypass' feature is for debug test builds only and must not be enabled in a release build` at `policy.rs:45` |
| `ci.yml` | parses with `python3` / PyYAML |

## Compatibility

- **Default builds:** the bypass is gone, and signing refuses namespaces other than `git`. git always passes `-n git`, so normal commit, tag and push signing is unaffected.
- **Library consumers (openvtc):** no API removed. `decide` and `check_namespace` are private.
- **`--all-features`:** in a debug profile it enables the bypass for tests. In a release profile it fails to compile, by design.

## Not in this PR: moving signing into the VTA

This PR makes the gate honest and removes the free pass. It does not change what code running as the user can obtain. That needs the follow-up:

- did-git-sign asks the VTA to sign the sshsig preimage (`VtaClient::sign`) instead of fetching the Ed25519 seed;
- the did-git-sign credential is provisioned with sign-only access to its one key (no secret export);
- every signature is recorded in the VTA's own audit log.

Signing then becomes revocable, server-audited and rate-limitable, and the seed never reaches the client.

## Note

The open release-pipeline PR also edits `ci.yml`: it pins actions, replaces the toolchain action with rustup and sets read-only permissions. The two edit different lines of the `test` job and merge cleanly. The steps added here use only `run:`.

title: fix(did): refuse to resolve a did:webvh hosted on a local-only name or non-public address
body:
## Why

The consent prompt resolves the `rpDid` a page supplies (`verifyDid`), and the vault panel resolves a principal DID to derive its signing key (`deriveSigningKeyId`). Resolving a did:webvh fetches its log from the host the DID names. Whoever wrote the DID chose that host, and this path deliberately runs with no host grant (see `host-permissions.ts`). So a page could make the extension send requests to loopback, the local network or a cloud metadata address while the prompt was open.

`didwebvh-ts` refuses plain dotted-quad and colon-form IPv6 literals. It does not refuse local-only names, or the other IPv4 spellings that the URL parser accepts and rewrites into a private address.

## Change

- New `packages/core/src/did/egress-guard.ts`. `assertResolvableWebvhHost(did)` works in three steps:
  - It takes the host with `didWebvhDomain` and percent-decodes it.
  - It parses the host with the WHATWG URL parser, the same parser the resolver uses to build its fetch URL. This strips the port and canonicalises numeric forms.
  - It throws `BlockedEndpointError` (`code: "E_BLOCKED_ENDPOINT"`, `reason: "private_address" | "private_name" | "invalid_url"`) for any of the following:
    - IPv4 outside public space: this-network, loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, IETF protocol assignments, documentation, benchmarking, multicast, reserved and broadcast.
    - IPv6 loopback and unspecified, ULA, link-local, site-local, multicast, documentation, and IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 forms (judged by the embedded IPv4 address).
    - `localhost`, `local`, `internal` and `home.arpa`, the names under them, and single-label names.
    - A host that does not parse, or that carries userinfo, a path, a query, a fragment, a second layer of percent-encoding, or whitespace.

  The guard does not use `didwebvh-ts`'s own IP check. Its ranges, names, error code and reason strings match `net-guard.js` in the next `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` release, so it can be swapped for that module once it ships.
- `verifyDid` and `deriveSigningKeyId` call the guard for did:webvh before resolving. A refusal comes back in each function's existing failure shape: `resolved: false` plus `error`, and `candidates: []` plus `error`. Neither function throws.
- Both functions gain an optional `{ resolveDid }` option, named like `VerifyTrustTaskProofOptions.resolveDid`, so tests can prove the resolver is never reached. Existing callers are unchanged.
- `host-permissions.ts`: the comment on the grant exemption for DID resolution now says the host is judged before anything is fetched.

## User-visible behaviour

- **Consent prompt:** a DID with a refused host shows the existing "Verification failed" badge. The detail line reads, for example: "Could not resolve this DID: the DID's host localhost is a local-network name, not a public internet host, so it was not contacted." No agent name is shown.
- **Vault panel:** the same message appears as the signing-key derivation error, and nothing is auto-filled.
- **Other screens:** `useAgentNames` shows no name, as for any DID that does not resolve.
- DIDs on public hosts behave as before.

## Not covered

- A public name that resolves to a private address. An extension has no DNS API, so this needs resolution somewhere that can see the address.
- Other resolution paths in `packages/core/src/didcomm/index.ts`: mediator, key agreement, and the `resolveDidDocument` that Trust-Task proof verification uses. Also not covered: nested did:webvh verification methods that `didwebvh-ts` fetches itself. These should move to the shared guard once `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` ships it.
- Approve in the consent window is still not gated on verification succeeding. That is unchanged here.
- `proxyFetch` and gateway registration.

## Tests

`packages/core/tests/did.egress-guard.mjs` (node:test):

- The guard refuses local-only names, alternate numeric IPv4 spellings, non-public IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and malformed hosts. It passes public names, including ones with a blocked word as a label (`localhost.example.com`), and addresses just outside the blocked ranges.
- `verifyDid` and `deriveSigningKeyId` return their failure shape for every refused host without calling an injected resolver. Both still call the resolver for a public host.
- With the real resolver and a recording `fetch`, refused hosts produce no request, while a public host does.

Results: every CI step passed locally on Node 26.7.0, starting from a cold build (no `dist` or build info):

- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- `npm test`: tsp-js 51, core 609, extension 590, reviewer-demo 9, with no failures
- the MV3 single-bundle and bundle-surface assertions
- Web Store packaging and the zip checks

The Node 24 leg of the matrix was not run locally.

To check the tests are not vacuous, the guard calls were removed from the built output. The three wiring tests then failed as expected.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new network call; the guard is synchronous
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a, no state
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; the bridge's VerifyRpDidResult is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no configuration; a host that cannot be parsed is refused
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the message says the host was not contacted
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — n/a, no mutation
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — R3.7: the stable code is on the thrown error, but only the message crosses the bridge; the UI renders it and does not branch on it
```

title: feat(vtc)!: vetter registry, grant resend, community branding and automatic vetter grants
body:
Stacked on #1429 (`feat/vtc-vetter-role-vec`). Draft — reviewed with the rest of the vetting stack.

The vetter role credential (#1429) names a vetter, but an applicant had no way to find one, a vetter who lost the credential could not get it back, and every vetter had to be named by hand. This implements the community side of the vetter registry — `CONTRACT-vetter-registry.md` §1–§8 — against the specs in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#453 (`spec/vetting-vetter-registry`).

## vta-sdk (breaking: `!`)

- `protocols::vetting` — `vtc/vetting/vetters/{profile,list,resend}/0.1`: URIs (+ `#response`), `VetterProfileBody` (`VetterLocation`, `VetterEvent`) → `VetterProfileResponseBody`; `VetterListBody` → `VetterListResponseBody` (`ListedVetter`); `VetterResendBody` → `VetterResendResponseBody`; `VETTING_VETTER_PROFILE_ERR_NOT_ELIGIBLE`, `VETTING_VETTER_RESEND_ERR_NOT_GRANTED`; bounds constants; `check_shape` on each. Admin REST shapes: `VetterGrantListResponse` / `VetterGrantRow` / `VetterProfileSummary` / `GrantOrigin`, and `AutoGrantConfig` / `AutoGrantStatus` / `AutoGrantSweep`.
- `protocols::join_requests` — `CommunityBranding` (+ `check_shape`, `is_empty`); `JoinRequestManifestResponseBody.branding`. **Breaking**: that struct is not `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- `vetting::ticket_uri` — `encode(&TicketUri) -> String`, `decode(&str) -> Result<TicketUri, VettingError>`.
- `vetting::status` — `check_credential_status(&Value, issuer, impl AsyncFn(&str) -> Result<Value, String>, &TrustTaskVmResolver) -> StatusCheck` (`Active | Revoked | Unknown(String)`). Verifies the list credential's proof (`assertionMethod`, signer = issuer), `issuer`, `id` = fetched URL, validity window and purpose; decodes with `affinidi-status-list` (the VTC's own encoder; new optional dep under `vetting`); index, entry count, URL and `encodedList` length and GZIP inflation are all bounded.
- `VettingError::UnsupportedVersion` (additive; `#[non_exhaustive]`).

## vtc-service

| Surface | What |
|---|---|
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1` | Active member with a live grant only (`…profile:notEligible`); whole replace; a document whose `issuedAt` is older than the stored profile's is refused (`malformedRequest`). New `vetter_profiles` keyspace (backed up). Deleted on grant revocation (endorsement revoke, auto-grant sweep) and on departure. |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/list/0.1` | Any identified caller (else `permissionDenied`); filters, one event satisfying every event filter, ended events never listed; ordering per spec; offset cursor bound to a digest of the filters. |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1` + `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/{memberDid}/resend` | Grant rows now keep the signed credential; delivered again. `…resend:notGranted` (404) / `unavailable` (503). |
| `GET/PUT /v1/community/branding` | Replace; `accentColor` stored lower case; `branding` on manifest 0.2 only. |
| `GET/PUT /v1/vetting/auto-grant` | `{enabled, sweepMinutes, validitySeconds}` + `lastSweep {ranAt, granted, revoked, errors}`. Sweeper wakes every minute. |
| policy purpose `vetterEligibility` | Package `vtc.vetter_eligibility`; input `{did, status, roles, tenureDays, admittedVia, underReview, depth}`; `allow` grants (origin auto), `deny` revokes only auto grants, anything else changes nothing. Default: active genesis members not under review. An admin granting an auto vetter adopts the grant. |
| `GET /v1/vetting/vetters` | Every grant: member, validity, revoked, live, origin, profile summary. |
| `GET /v1/join-requests/{id}/vetting` | The vetting facts a request was decided on (now recorded beside it), with `withdrawnNow` per statement. |
| `GET /v1/vetting/revocations` | Withdrawal notices with affected join requests / members and `reviewState`. |

Also: DIDComm/TSP dispatch of the three tasks; grant delivery moved out of `GRANT_LOCK` (a network send no longer holds up every grant, revocation and profile write — this includes #1429's admin grant path); census count for `spec/vtc/vetting/` 2 → 5; payload ext census entries; keyspace census 29 → 30; OpenAPI snapshot and admin-ui `wire.ts` / `wire-types.ts` regenerated; `policies-api.ts` purpose list.

vti-common: `AuditEvent::{VetterAutoGranted, VetterProfileUpdated, VetterProfileDeleted, VetterGrantResent, VetterAutoGrantConfigured, VetterAutoGrantSwept, CommunityBrandingUpdated}` (additive; `#[non_exhaustive]`).

Docs: `docs/03-vtc/vetting.md` (sections 4–6, admin views, limits), `architecture.md`, `backup-restore.md`.

## Test evidence (local — stacked PRs get no CI)

Isolated target dir, `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1` unless noted.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` | 4183 passed, 0 failed, 50 ignored |
| `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` | 1590 passed, 7 failed, 1 ignored. Six are the tests that need the embedded admin UI (`admin_ui::tests` ×4, `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_*` ×2); the seventh was `openapi_snapshot`, stale by one doc comment edited after the run — both covered below |
| the six UI tests again **without** `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` | pass (`--lib admin_ui` 8 passed, `routing_modes` admin 3 passed) |
| `UPDATE_OPENAPI=1 cargo test -p vtc-service --test openapi_snapshot`, then the same without it | regenerated (diff: `PolicyPurpose` description only); 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |
| `cargo check --workspace --locked` | ok |
| `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client,vetting --lib vetting` (CI feature-combo step) | 81 passed |
| `cargo test -p vta-sdk --all-features` | 1023 passed |
| admin-ui `npx tsc -b --noEmit`, `npm run wire:check` | clean |
| `scripts/check-lockfile-self-pins.sh`, `check-authz-context-types.sh`, `check-nitro-copies-every-member.py`, `check-workspace-version-reqs.py` | pass |

Not run: the `didcomm-harness` tests (`join_tsp`, `registry_didcomm`), which need a live mediator.

New tests: `vetting::status` (hostile entries and lists, forged/tampered/expired lists, GZIP bomb bound, fetch-once), `vetting::ticket_uri` (round trips, version, both/half tickets, hostile input), profile/list/resend/auto-grant shape and serde closure, listing filter/order/cursor units, sweep facts/depth/decision units, branding storage; integration in `tests/join_requests.rs` (publish + find, paging with filter-bound cursors, unidentified caller refused, notEligible, unlist + revoke deletes, stale document, resend notGranted/unavailable over task and admin REST, branding on manifest 0.2 only, sweep grants/revokes only its own, adoption, vetting facts + revocations + underReview) and `tests/ceremony_execute.rs` (departure deletes the profile).

## Deviations from the contract

Names, bounds, error codes and SDK function names follow the contract and the #453 specs. Where the implementation had to choose:

- **Policy purpose naming.** The contract's `vetter_eligibility` is the Rego package (`vtc.vetter_eligibility`); the purpose's wire name is `vetterEligibility`, like every other `PolicyPurpose` (`roleChange` → `vtc.role_change`).
- **Extra policy fact.** The input also carries `did`, so a community can write a rule about a specific member. The six contract facts are exactly as named; `depth` is present and `null` when unknown.
- **`errors` in the last sweep is a count**, not a list; per-member reasons go to the log.
- **`admittedVia` derivation** (the contract names the values, not the rule): `vetting` when the admitting join request's recorded vetting facts were satisfied by counted statements, else `invitation` when the member joined on an invitation, else `open` for any other approved join request, else `genesis`. `underReview` = a statement counted toward the admission has since been withdrawn. `depth` = 0 for genesis, 1 + shallowest counted vetter, else `null`.
- **Admin REST routes have no Trust Task binding** (`GET /v1/vetting/vetters`, `GET/PUT /v1/vetting/auto-grant`, `GET /v1/vetting/revocations`, `GET /v1/join-requests/{id}/vetting`, `GET/PUT /v1/community/branding`): no spec URI exists for them, so they are mounted like the schemas routes rather than borrowing an unrelated URI. `POST …/{memberDid}/resend` enforces `vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1`.
- **"Withdrawal notices, with review state"** has no stored review workflow: `reviewState` is derived (`needsReview` when a current member was admitted with the statement counted, else `noAdmission`), plus `affectedJoinRequests` / `affectedMembers`.
- **Vetting facts are now persisted** beside each decided join request (`join_vetting:<id>` in `join_requests`, deleted with the request) — needed for `GET /v1/join-requests/{id}/vetting`, `admittedVia` and the revocations view. Requests decided before this change have none.
- **Resend of a grant made before this change** (no stored credential) answers `notGranted` with a message to revoke and grant again.
- **Profile staleness:** the specification's MAY (refuse a document older than the stored one's `issuedAt`) is implemented.
- **Listing cursor** is an opaque offset bound to a digest of the filters; a profile published or withdrawn between pages can shift one entry across a page boundary.
- **Retry safety:** `vta_sdk::retry_safety` classifies only the VTA's catalog (`trust_tasks::ALL_URIS`), which contains no `spec/vtc/*` task — #1429's grant is not in it either — so there is no census entry to add. Classification for the record: profile retry-safe (idempotent replace), list read-only, resend retry-safe.
- **Manual grant of an auto vetter adopts the grant** (origin becomes manual) — the contract says the sweep revokes only its own; this makes an admin's explicit grant stick.

## Not done here

- Admin-ui panels and `cnm` commands (contract §8 UI, §9) — follow-up agents, on these endpoints and wire types.
- Manifest criteria editor validation + digest display (§8, UI).
- The mediator-backed `--features didcomm-harness` tests (`join_tsp`, `registry_didcomm`) need a live mediator and were not run.

title: feat(vtc)!: vetter registry, grant resend, community branding and automatic vetter grants (#1430)
body:
feat(vtc)!: vetter registry, grant resend, community branding and automatic vetter grants (#1430)

* feat(vtc)!: vetter registry, grant resend, community branding and automatic vetter grants

The vetter role credential (#1429) names a vetter, but an applicant had no way
to find one, a vetter who lost the credential could not get it back, and every
vetter had to be named by hand. This adds the community side of the vetter
registry: CONTRACT-vetter-registry §1–§8, as specified in
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#453.

vta-sdk:
- protocols::vetting — vtc/vetting/vetters/{profile,list,resend}/0.1: URIs
  (+ #response), VetterProfileBody (VetterLocation, VetterEvent) →
  VetterProfileResponseBody, VetterListBody → VetterListResponseBody
  (ListedVetter), VetterResendBody → VetterResendResponseBody, the
  profile:notEligible and resend:notGranted codes, bounds constants and
  check_shape. Admin REST shapes VetterGrantListResponse (VetterGrantRow,
  VetterProfileSummary, GrantOrigin) and AutoGrantConfig / AutoGrantStatus /
  AutoGrantSweep. VettingMethod derives ToSchema under `openapi`.
- protocols::join_requests — CommunityBranding, and `branding` on
  JoinRequestManifestResponseBody.
- vetting::ticket_uri — encode/decode of the `vetting-ticket:` URI a vetter's
  QR code carries.
- vetting::status — check_credential_status: fetch the status list through the
  caller's fetch, verify its Data Integrity proof, issuer and id, decode the
  bitstring with affinidi-status-list (the crate the VTC encodes with) and read
  the bit. Every index, length and inflation is bounded.
- VettingError::UnsupportedVersion.

vtc-service:
- vtc/vetting/vetters/profile/0.1: only an active member holding a live grant
  (notEligible otherwise); replaces the profile; a document older than the
  stored one's issuedAt is refused. New `vetter_profiles` keyspace, backed up.
  A profile is deleted when the vetter's grant is revoked (endorsement revoke,
  the sweep) or they depart.
- vtc/vetting/vetters/list/0.1: any identified caller; language, country,
  region, city, method and event filters, one event satisfying every event
  filter, ended events never listed; ordered as the specification orders;
  offset cursors bound to the filters.
- vtc/vetting/vetters/resend/0.1 and POST /v1/vetting/vetters/{memberDid}/resend:
  grant rows now keep the signed credential, which is delivered again;
  notGranted, or unavailable when the delivery cannot be handed to transport.
- GET/PUT /v1/community/branding; `branding` on manifest 0.2 only.
- Automatic grants: policy purpose `vetterEligibility` (package
  vtc.vetter_eligibility) over status, roles, tenureDays, admittedVia,
  underReview and depth; a sweeper that runs when enabled
  (GET/PUT /v1/vetting/auto-grant, last sweep kept); grants it issues are
  marked auto and it revokes only those; an admin granting an automatic vetter
  adopts the grant. The shipped policy names active genesis members not under
  review.
- The vetting facts a join request was decided on are recorded beside it;
  GET /v1/join-requests/{id}/vetting reads them, and GET /v1/vetting/revocations
  lists withdrawal notices with the admissions they touch.
- GET /v1/vetting/vetters: every grant, with origin and profile summary.
- The three tasks dispatch over REST documents, DIDComm and TSP. Census counts,
  the OpenAPI snapshot and the admin-ui wire types are updated.

vti-common: AuditEvent::{VetterAutoGranted, VetterProfileUpdated,
VetterProfileDeleted, VetterGrantResent, VetterAutoGrantConfigured,
VetterAutoGrantSwept, CommunityBrandingUpdated}.

Breaking in vta-sdk: JoinRequestManifestResponseBody gains `branding` and is not
#[non_exhaustive]. The new VettingError variant and AuditEvent variants are
additive (#[non_exhaustive]).

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs(vtc): eligibleVetters.role is a bare token

The vetting guide said eligibleVetters.role could be "custom:vetter". Both the normative join-requests/manifest/0.2 schema (pattern ^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$) and shape::role refuse a colon. The role is the one named in the community's CommunityRole credential — a bare token such as "vetter" — not an ACL custom:* role name.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc): a vetter granted in the second they joined holds a live grant

A grant's created_at is its credential's validFrom, written to the second; a member's joined_at keeps sub-seconds. is_live_for compared grant.created_at >= member.joined_at, so a grant made in the same second the member joined sorted before the membership: it never read as live, granting again issued a duplicate credential on a second status-list slot, and the listing reported the member as holding no live grant. vetter_eligible made the same comparison, so that vetter's statements would never have counted, and its joined_at > issued_at check against a statement's second-precision validFrom had the same shape.

Membership start is now compared at whole seconds through one helper (vetters::joined_at_second / recorded_during_membership), used by is_live_for (and so live_grant, live_grants and the grant path) and by both checks in vetter_eligible.

Regression tests: a unit test that a grant stamped with the member's joining second is live while one from the second before is not, and join_requests::a_vetter_named_in_the_second_they_joined_is_not_granted_twice, which grants twice to a member who joined late in the current second and requires the same endorsement back and one grant row.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc): name vetters with a revocable vetter role credential
body:
Stacked on #1428 (`feat/vtc-vetting-revocation`). A vetter was a member holding the ACL role `custom:vetter`. That is an access-control fact only the community can see: an applicant had no way to know a vetter's statement would count, and the ACL keeps no history, so "held the role when signing" was approximated. This names vetters with a **vetter role credential** instead — issued by the community, recorded, revocable, delivered to the member, verified at join, and presentable to an applicant.

## vta-sdk

`protocols::vetting` (serde, always compiled):

- `COMMUNITY_ROLE_ENDORSEMENT_TYPE = "CommunityRole"`, `VETTER_ROLE = "vetter"`
- `VETTING_VETTER_GRANT_TYPE` = `https://trusttasks.org/spec/vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`, `VETTING_VETTER_GRANT_RESPONSE_TYPE` (`#response`)
- `role_matches(held, required)`: `vetter` ≡ `custom:vetter` in either direction, otherwise exact
- `VetterGrantBody { memberDid, validitySeconds?, ext? }` (closed, `check_shape`: a DID, one day to two years) and `VetterGrantResponseBody { endorsementId, credentialId, validFrom, validUntil, ext? }`
- `MIN_/MAX_/DEFAULT_VETTER_GRANT_VALIDITY_SECONDS`

`vetting::eligibility` (feature `vetting`):

- `community_role(&Value) -> Option<(communityDid, role)>`
- `build_eligibility_vp(holder, credentials, challenge, domain)`: the `vetting/request#response` `eligibilityVp` (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#452, request rule 5): `nonce` = the request document's `id`, `domain` = its `joinDid`, `eddsa-jcs-2022`, purpose `authentication`
- `verify_eligibility_vp(vp, &EligibilityExpectations { vetter, community, role, challenge, domain, now }, resolver) -> VerifiedEligibility`. It checks:
  - the VP proof, with signer = holder = vetter;
  - `nonce` and `domain` match the request `id` and `joinDid`;
  - the VP carries a role credential issued by the community, naming the vetter, for that community, in a matching role;
  - that credential's proof, by the issuer (`assertionMethod`);
  - that credential's window, allowing for clock skew.
- The status list is left to the caller, via `credential_status()`.
- New `VettingError::NoRoleCredential` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`).

## vtc-service

- **Grant**: `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant/0.1`, as `POST /v1/vetting/vetters` and as a Trust Task document (dispatcher, so REST `/v1/trust-tasks`, DIDComm and TSP). Both go through `vetting::vetters::grant`:
  - **Auth:** Admin, read from the ACL row. The subject must be a current member.
  - **Credential:** allocates a revocation slot and issues the VEC (`urn:uuid` id, `credentialStatus`, one year by default).
  - **Record:** stores an `Endorsement` row (`CommunityRole`, `{role: "vetter"}`, `validUntil`).
  - **Audit:** `VetterGranted` + `VecIssued`.
  - **Delivery:** best effort.
  - **Converges:** while a grant is live, it is returned (200) instead of a second being issued (201).
- **Revoke**: unchanged — `vtc/endorsements/revoke/0.1` already accepts any row.
- **Departure** revokes the member's grants (flip + mark) and reports them on `DepartOutcome.revoked_grants`. Both leave paths audit `CustomEndorsementRevoked` + `StatusListFlipped`.
- **Eligibility at submit**: the ACL check is gone. A statement counts only when:
  - its issuer is a current member who joined by the statement's `validFrom`;
  - they hold a `CommunityRole` grant for the role that was recorded during this membership and by `validFrom`;
  - that grant was unexpired then and is not revoked now.
- `Endorsement` rows gain `validUntil`; the endorsement list/show now report `issued.expiresAt` from it.
- admin-ui: member page gets a "Vetter role" card — grant, show the live grant, revoke.

Censuses: manifest `spec/vtc/vetting/` 1 → 2, dispatched URIs, audit event names, OpenAPI snapshot + `wire.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client,vetting --lib vetting`
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib`
- [x] `cargo test -p vtc-service --test join_requests --test endorsements --test ceremony_execute --test openapi_snapshot --test trust_task_manifest`
- [x] `cargo test -p vti-common --lib audit`
- [x] `cargo clippy -p vtc-service -p vta-sdk -p vti-common --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- [x] admin-ui `npx tsc -b --noEmit`

title: feat(vtc): let a vetter withdraw a vetting statement
body:
Stacked on #1427.

A vetter can now **withdraw a vetting statement** they issued, and a withdrawn statement stops counting. This implements OpenVTC `docs/design/vetting-process.md` §9.6 (decision D18).

## Why here, and not a status list

The VTA's `credentials/revoke` only marks its local record, so nothing a verifier reads would change. A status list per vetter would also be a poor fit: one holding a handful of one vetter's statements gives no herd privacy (VTI-CRD-011/012).

The party that relies on a statement is the community, so the vetter tells the community directly. VTA-hosted status lists shared across issuers remain the V1 answer, for when statements have to be checked outside their community.

## What it does

- **Trust Task:** `vtc/vetting/revoke-statement/0.1` is served over the document endpoint, DIDComm and TSP. The payload is `{statementId, statementDigestMultibase, reason?}` and the response is `{recordedAt}`.
- **Who can withdraw what:** a notice is keyed by the **authenticated sender**, the statement id and the digest, and counts only against a presented statement with all three.
  - So a notice can only ever withdraw a statement its sender signed. A notice about someone else's statement is recorded under the wrong issuer and matches nothing; a test pins this.
  - The digest is compared on its decoded bytes (`dtg_credentials::decode_digest_multibase`), as DTG Credentials requires.
- **Senders must be members.** Vetters are members, and this keeps the store from becoming a sink anyone on the network can write to.
- **Idempotent:** a repeated notice returns the original `recordedAt` and writes nothing.
- **Audited:** the first recording writes a new `AuditEvent::VettingStatementRevoked` (vti-common; the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so this isn't breaking). The actor is the vetter, and the payload carries the statement id, digest and reason.
- **Durable:** notices get a new `vetting_revocations` keyspace, which is **backed up**. A withdrawn statement must stay withdrawn across a restore. It is added to `ALL`, `BACKED_UP`, `backed_up_handle`, `AppState` and the test fixture, with the keyspace and backup censuses updated.
- **Counted:** `vetting_facts` now reads `revoked` from the store in place of the placeholder `false`. The existing counting rule already refuses a revoked statement, reporting `revoked`.

## Tests

- **`vetting::revocation::tests`:**
  - a notice withdraws only its own issuer's statement, and not a different credential reusing the id;
  - repeating a notice keeps the first recording time;
  - a malformed digest is refused and names nothing;
  - an empty id is refused.
- **`tests/join_requests.rs`**, end to end:
  - Carol withdraws her statement, and the application drops to `requestMore` / `vetting:statements:1`;
  - a notice from Erin about Carol's statement changes nothing, and the application is still `allow`;
  - a non-member's notice is refused.
- **Censuses:** the vti-common audit event census includes the new variant; the keyspace count moves 28 → 29; the backup partition and handle census, the dispatcher census and `trust_task_manifest` all pass. The `spec/vtc/vetting/` unpublished count stays 1, since it's the same URI.

## Not in this PR (documented in `docs/03-vtc/vetting.md`)

- **No retention sweep:** notices are kept indefinitely.
- **No post-admission review:** a withdrawal after admission is recorded and audited, but doesn't open a review of the membership it helped grant. That arrives with the lineage/cascade-review work in V1.

title: feat(vtc): count vetting statements in the join decision
body:
Stacked on #1426.

The community now **counts presented vetting statements when it decides a join**. Before this, join policy had no way to see them. This is the decision half of vetted admission (OpenVTC `docs/design/vetting-process.md` §10).

## What the host establishes

The raw submit path verifies the VP's holder binding and none of the credentials inside it, so nothing here trusts a statement just because it arrived. `vtc-service/src/vetting/mod.rs` checks each identity-vetting `EndorsementCredential` in the join VP:

1. **Verifies it** with `vta_sdk::vetting::statement::verify_statement`: proof by the issuer, credential type, bounded validity and a strict endorsement body. Proofs by a `did:webvh` issuer resolve through the VTC's DID cache (`AppState::trust_task_vm_resolver`).
2. **Binds it to the applicant:** the statement's subject must be the proven holder.
3. **Checks vetter eligibility:** the issuer is a current member holding the role `eligibleVetters.role` names (`vetter` matches `custom:vetter`), had joined before issuing, and has an ACL entry that hasn't lapsed.
4. **Counts the survivors** with `vta_sdk::vetting::requirements::evaluate`, the same rule the applicant's client uses for its checklist. Distinct vetters are distinct *members* (VTI-CMP-070).

The criterion applied is the one whose current `requirementsDigest` the applicant sent in `extensions`; failing that, the first vetting criterion. The result goes to the join policy as `input.evidence.vetting`: per-statement verdicts with stable failure codes, counts, `commitments_consistent`, `independence_ok`, `satisfied` and `needs`.

## What the default policy decides

When vetting is required, **neither an invitation nor a trusted credential bypasses it**. There are four mutually exclusive vetting outcomes:

| Facts | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Vetters verified different identity commitments | `refer` → `vetting-review` |
| Still short | `request_more`, needs `["vetting"]` |
| Enough, but a relationship cap is exceeded | `refer` → `vetting-review` |
| Met, but an invitation is required and absent | `request_more`, needs `["vetting:invitation"]` |

With vetting met, the request is admitted as `member`, or at the invited role if a valid invitation is present. With no vetting facts, the default behaves exactly as before; a test pins that.

**The needs string.** A visually authored policy has a static `with`, so it can only say `needs: ["vetting"]`. After `decide`, `decide_join` expands that into the precise shortfall, e.g. `vetting:statements:1`. That is what the applicant's status poll then shows.

**Visual editor.** The admin console's rule-IR catalogue (`admin-ui/src/lib/rule-ir.ts`) gains the matching conditions:
- `vetting_inconsistent`
- `vetting_incomplete`
- `vetting_not_independent`
- `vetting_invitation_missing`
- `vetting_satisfied`
- `vetting_ok`

Each comes with its helper Rego and a client-side mirror. The default `join.rego`'s `@vtc-rule-ir` header is regenerated from those routes, so the editor renders it and can recompile it.

## Also

- **`Evidence` gains a `vetting` slot.** The other eight constructors pass `None`.
- **Credential-exchange `present` path:** passes no vetting facts yet; this is recorded in the operator doc's limits.
- **New operator guide:** `docs/03-vtc/vetting.md` covers registering the type and a criterion, naming vetters, what is checked, and the default decisions and limits.

## Tests

- **`vetting::tests`:** criterion selection by digest and fallback, role spellings, needs expansion, and statement pick-out.
- **`policy::default::tests`:** each vetting outcome; an invitation and a trusted credential each fail to bypass required vetting; a required invitation is asked for once vetting is met; an invited role holds with vetting met; behaviour without vetting facts is unchanged.
- **`tests/join_requests.rs`**, end to end over `POST /v1/trust-tasks` with real signed statements:
  - two eligible vetters → `allow` and the applicant is admitted;
  - one statement → `requestMore` on the wire (`request_more` in Rego), with needs exactly `["vetting:statements:1"]`;
  - a statement from a member without the vetter role doesn't count.
- **Local runs:** the full `vtc-service` lib suite (981 passed), `join_requests`, `openapi_snapshot`, `trust_task_manifest`, `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `tsc -b --noEmit` for the console.

## Known limits (V0, documented)

- **Role history:** "held the vetter role when issuing" is approximated by "holds it now and had joined by then". The ACL keeps no role history, so a demoted vetter's statements stop counting.
- **Withdrawn statements:** `revoked` is always `false` until the revocation-notice change later in this stack.
- **`requirementsGrace`:** not yet applied. `applicant_digest_matches: false` is surfaced so a policy can act on it.

The raw submit path verifies none of the credentials inside the VP, so each
statement is verified here: proof by its issuer, bound to the proven holder,
issued by a current member holding the vetter role who had joined before
issuing. Survivors are counted with vta_sdk's evaluate, the same rule the
applicant's checklist uses; distinct vetters are distinct members
(VTI-CMP-070). The result reaches join policy as input.evidence.vetting.

The default join.rego gains four mutually exclusive vetting outcomes, and
neither an invitation nor a trusted credential bypasses required vetting.
A visually authored policy can only return needs ["vetting"]; decide_join
expands that into the precise shortfall. The admin console's rule-IR
catalogue carries the same conditions, and the default's IR header is
regenerated from them. Without vetting facts the default is unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vtc): write vetting values and needs in lowerCamelCase

Follows vta-sdk's alignment with the Trust Task specs: `inPerson` in requirements, facts and the `vetting:method:inPerson:<n>` needs grammar, in tests and in docs/03-vtc/vetting.md.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(vtc): advertise vetting requirements in the join manifest
body:
Stacked on #1425.

A community can now **advertise what vetting it requires** before anyone applies. This is the first VTC half of vetted admission (OpenVTC `docs/design/vetting-process.md` §6).

## What changes

- **Stored criteria carry vetting requirements.**
  - `AcceptsCriterion` gains an optional `vetting` (`vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::VettingRequirements`).
  - `store_accepts` refuses requirements that `VettingRequirements::validate` says no applicant could satisfy: `minStatements: 0`, a method floor on a method that isn't accepted, or a month-based duration.
  - `POST /v1/schemas/accepts` additionally refuses a `statementType` that isn't a registered endorsement type, where the operator can act on the error. Otherwise it would only surface at an applicant's submit.
- **Manifest 0.2.**
  - `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` is served beside 0.1: over the Trust Task document endpoint, over DIDComm, and in `DISPATCHED_URIS`.
  - A 0.2 criterion carries its `vetting` object and a `requirementsDigest`, computed over the criterion **exactly as delivered** minus the digest itself. An applicant recomputes it with `vta_sdk::vetting::requirements::requirements_digest` and records it when it starts gathering statements, so a mid-application change is detectable (design §6.3).
  - A 0.1 answer keeps its own shape and carries neither member. The version the document names decides.

Every number in the requirements is the community's policy (design D15). There are no defaults here, and documentation is left to each vetter unless a community sets `acceptedDocumentClasses` (D16).

## Not in this PR

- **Counting presented vetting statements:** the next PR in the stack does this. It adds verification into facts and the `join.rego` module.
- **Admin console form for `vetting`:** the API accepts it, and the console can follow.

## Tests

- **`routes::join_requests::manifest::tests`:**
  - a 0.1 answer carries no vetting members;
  - a 0.2 digest recomputes from what the applicant receives;
  - changing the requirements changes the digest;
  - a criterion without vetting still gets a 0.2 digest.
- **`schemas::accepts::tests`:** evaluable requirements round-trip, and unsatisfiable ones are refused and not stored.
- **`tests/join_requests.rs::manifest_0_2_advertises_vetting_requirements_and_their_digest`:** end to end over `POST /v1/trust-tasks`, for both versions.
- **Dispatcher census:** `dispatcher_routes_every_dispatched_uri` lists the new URI.

Run locally, all green:
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib -- manifest accepts dispatcher`
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test join_requests manifest`
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest`
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

`../design-docs/` isn't available in this checkout, so the vti-stack-development-guide checklist isn't pasted. This PR adds a read to an existing public task and no outbound call.

title: feat(vta-sdk)!: wire types and crypto for peer identity vetting
body:
Adds the shared wire types and crypto for **peer identity vetting** in `vta-sdk`. This is how an applicant gets vetted by existing members before joining a community, replacing the Linux kernel's PGP web of trust.

Design: OpenVTC `docs/design/vetting-process.md` (OpenVTC/openvtc#292). This PR is the base of the VTI stack. Nothing serves or sends these tasks yet; the VTC and OpenVTC PRs build on it.

## What's in it

### `protocols::vetting` (serde only, always compiled)

- Type URIs and payloads for `vetting/request/0.1`, `vetting/session/0.1`, `vetting/decline/0.1` and `vtc/vetting/revoke-statement/0.1`.
- `VettingRequirements`, the per-criterion object a community advertises in its join manifest.
  - Every number in it is **community policy**; this crate supplies no defaults (design D15).
  - `acceptedDocumentClasses` is optional and absent by default, because each vetter decides what documentation they accept (D16).
  - `validate()` refuses requirements that cannot be evaluated: `minStatements: 0`, a method floor on a method that is never accepted, or a calendar-dependent duration such as `P4M`.
- `VettingCard` (an r-card VDS) and `IdentityVettingEndorsement` (the Vetting Statement's `endorsement` body).
- A refusal to vet is a framework `trust-task-error` with a `vetting/request:*` code, never a `#response` carrying an outcome.
- **Aligned with the Trust Task specs** (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, follow-up commit):
  - every enum and documentation value is lowerCamelCase (SPEC §4.10): `inPerson`, `priorAcquaintance`, `sameEmployer`, `nationalId`;
  - `check_shape` on each payload enforces the schema bounds and patterns serde cannot: lengths, the Crockford ticket-code alphabet, 32-byte base64url challenges, secrets and salts, BCP 47 language tags, URI statement ids, `did:` members, and no `person.portrait`;
  - `VettingRequirements::validate` adds `MAJOR.MINOR` versions, role names, https governance URLs and the 32-character duration cap;
  - cards and statements are shape-checked both before signing and on receipt. `RequestShapeError` is now `ShapeError`.

### `vetting` module (feature `vetting`)

Every verifier returns a `Verified*` type (typestate rule).

- **`card`:**
  - `sign_card` builds and signs the card. The signer must be the publisher, and validity is capped at 15 minutes.
  - `verify_card` checks audience, publisher, community, challenge and domain, then the time window, the proof by the publisher, required claims, and that the identity commitment recomputes.
  - The **identity commitment** is a salted digest over the required claims. The salt is per application and is disclosed to vetters but never to the community, so the community can check that every vetter verified the same identity without learning it (cf. dtgwg-cred-spec#38).
- **`statement`:**
  - `sign_statement` builds a DTG `EndorsementCredential` through `dtg-credentials`, with `taskContext` naming the session.
  - `verify_statement` parses strictly and requires an `id`, a `taskContext` and a bounded `validUntil`.
  - `check_against_card` lets the applicant confirm a statement was issued over the card they actually presented.
- **`requirements`:**
  - `evaluate` is the one counting rule, shared by the applicant's checklist and the community's policy facts. It counts distinct vetters by *member* rather than by DID (D14), applies method floors and relationship caps, checks commitments are consistent, and records per-statement not-counted reasons.
  - `Need::to_wire` defines the `needs` string grammar (`vetting:statements:<n>`, `vetting:method:<m>:<n>`), so the published verdict shape doesn't change.
  - `requirements_digest` computes the digest over a manifest criterion.
- **`match_code`:** same construction as the personhood match code, with its own domain tag (`vetting-session-match/v1\0`). A test pins that the two never collide.

### Manifest 0.2

`ManifestCriterion` gains optional `vetting` and `requirementsDigest` members. It is a published struct with no `#[non_exhaustive]`, hence the `!`. The VTC fills these in later in the stack; here the two literals set `None`.

## Census and CI

- **`payload_ext_census`:** `VettingCard`, `CardClaim` and `IdentityVettingEndorsement` are added to `NO_EXT_BY_DESIGN`. They are signed or attested content rather than payload roots, and closing them is the point: a member the verifier can't show or interpret would be signed anyway. The payloads that carry them keep `ext`.
- **`trust_task_manifest`:** three counted `UNPUBLISHED_CANONICAL_OK` entries (`spec/vetting/` ×3, `spec/vtc/vetting/` ×1, `manifest/0.2` ×1) cover the URIs bound ahead of their specs. The specs are proposed in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, and each count goes to zero when the trust-tasks-rs release that serves it is taken.
- **CI:** new step `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client,vetting --lib vetting`. `vetting` is off by default, so the workspace test job never compiled these tests. `client` is included because `trust_task_proof`'s own unit tests need it under `proof-verify`, which is an existing gap this PR doesn't widen.

## Run locally

- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features client,vetting --lib vetting`: 41 passed
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --no-fail-fast`
- `cargo test -p vtc-service --test trust_task_manifest`
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy -p vtc-service --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

## Design notes for review

- **Signing is done by the holder, as the persona DID.** `sign_card` and `sign_statement` take the persona's assertionMethod `Secret` (`did:webvh:…#key-N`), which OpenVTC loads for every persona — derived, imported or VTA-managed — and already uses for reciprocal VMCs, capability grants and personhood proofs. The proof names the persona's verification method, and verification resolves it through the DID document. The VTA's signing tasks don't fit (`keys/derive-and-sign-document` signs as a derived `did:key`; `keys/sign` is domain-separated), and aren't needed. Because the holder has the key, a VTA step-up can't gate the signature: V0 gates it with a client confirmation, recorded as D19.
- **Card digest** uses DTG Digest Encoding: JCS over the card without `proof`.
- **Relationship to trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#47:** that PR proposes replacing `EndorsementCredential` with a new statement type. If it lands, only `statement.rs`'s builder and type check move; the endorsement body carries over.

`../design-docs/` isn't available in this checkout, so the vti-stack-development-guide checklist isn't pasted here. This PR adds no service call.

title: Require confirmation for pairing, validate the push gateway URL, re-enable ATS
body:
### Summary

This tightens how the app decides who it trusts and where it sends its push token.

- **Pairing now needs confirmation.** Scanning a pairing code or saving the VTA in Settings no longer applies the change straight away. A confirmation sheet comes first.
- **The push gateway URL is validated**, and the gateway request no longer follows redirects.
- **App Transport Security is back at its defaults** in every configuration.
- **Sign-ins are no longer auto-approved unless you turn it on.** A new "Auto-approve sign-ins" setting controls this, and it never applies in the background.
- **The APNs token is no longer logged.**

Four commits, one per change. Each can be reviewed or reverted on its own, except that the pairing commit uses the gateway URL policy from the first commit.

### Behaviour changes

**1. Push gateway URL validation and ATS** (`fix: validate the push gateway URL and refuse redirects`)
- New `GatewayURLPolicy` in the package. It requires:
  - https;
  - no userinfo, query or fragment;
  - port absent or 443;
  - a DNS host name.
- The following hosts are refused:
  - IP literals in any spelling, including decimal, hex, octal and shorthand IPv4, and IPv6;
  - single-label names;
  - local-only suffixes (`localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.lan`, `.arpa`, `.svc`, …).
- A host outside the paired VTA's `did:web`/`did:webvh` domain is a **warning** (`hostNotBoundToVta`), shown in Settings and on the pairing sheet. It is not a refusal.
- The URL is checked when it is written (pairing, Settings) and again before the POST.
- `GatewayClient` takes an injectable `URLSession`. The default session is ephemeral, has a 15 s timeout, and keeps no cookies, cache or credentials. Redirects are refused, both on the session and per task.
- `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` is removed from `project.yml`. No local-networking exception was added, because the VTA and mediator are reached by the engine, not `URLSession`.
- `ios-app-build` now fails if any `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads*` key appears in the generated `Info.plist`.

**2. Pairing review and confirmation** (`feat: review and confirm pairings before applying them`)
- `PairingPayload.parse` accepts only `cierge-pair://`. The raw-JSON form is removed.
- New `PairingPolicy` in the package:
  - The mediator is taken from the VTA's DID document. A mediator in the code is only cross-checked, and a mismatch is refused.
  - A DID document with no mediator is refused.
  - The gateway must pass `GatewayURLPolicy`.
- `AgentModel.applyPairing` is replaced by two steps:
  - `stagePairing` resolves the DID document, runs the policy and shows `PairingConfirmSheet`. It saves nothing and does not connect.
  - `confirmPairing` applies the change.
- When the pairing replaces a **different** VTA, `confirmPairing`:
  - requires device-owner authentication (biometrics or passcode, via an injectable `DeviceOwnerAuthenticator`);
  - disconnects;
  - discards pending approvals and task consents;
  - turns push wake off;
  - then saves and connects.
- The sheet shows the VTA DID with its verified name, the domain, the mediator, the gateway host and the stated tenant. A red banner appears when the pairing replaces a different VTA.
- Settings no longer saves on every keystroke. VTA DID and gateway edits are drafts until **Save**, which goes through the same review. The mediator field is now read-only.
- Removed `resolveFromDid` and `saveConfig`.
- Added `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.

**3. Sign-in auto-approve setting** (`feat: ask before approving sign-ins; never approve in the background`)
- New `StepUpPolicy.decide` in the package. A step-up is auto-approved only if all three hold:
  - it has no authorization context;
  - the app is active;
  - **Settings → Behaviour → Auto-approve sign-ins** is on.
- Everything else is queued for Approve/Deny with a notification.
- A background push wake always passes `appActive: false`, so it only queues.

**4. APNs token logging** (`fix: stop logging the APNs device token`)
- The token `print` is removed.
- The Test tab's token row is DEBUG-only and shows an 8-character prefix.
- Engine log directives are `warn` in non-DEBUG builds.

### Product decisions to confirm

- **"Auto-approve sign-ins" defaults to off.** Existing users will be asked to approve every sign-in until they turn it on.
- **Re-pairing to a different VTA requires device-owner authentication.** A device with no passcode set cannot replace its VTA.
- **The gateway domain check is a warning, not a block.** Gateways run by a different domain than the VTA remain possible after the operator sees the warning.
- **A VTA whose DID document advertises no `#vta-didcomm` mediator can no longer be paired.** Manual mediator entry is gone.
- **The Test tab no longer shows or copies the full APNs token.**

### Upgrade notes

- Existing pairings are not re-prompted.
- A previously saved gateway URL that breaks a hard rule, such as `http://` or an IP address, is refused when push is registered, with a message in the Test tab. Re-save it in Settings.

### Not in this PR

- Signed pairing offers and nonce-bound enrolment.
- DID-addressed push gateway.
- Keychain accessibility changes for the holder key.
- Push-wake rate limiting.

### Testing

- **New package tests** (iOS Simulator, `VtaMobileAgent-Package`):
  - `GatewayURLPolicyTests`
  - `GatewayClientTests` (a `URLProtocol` stub answering 307)
  - `PairingPolicyTests`
  - `StepUpPolicyTests`
  - one new case in `StepUpTests`
  - `testParsesRawJson` replaced by `testRejectsRawJson`
- **App-target logic is not unit-tested.** `stagePairing`, `confirmPairing` and the `appActive` wiring are kept as thin glue around the package policies, because the app target has no test bundle.
- **Pre-CI checks** (a host without Xcode):
  - The pure package files and their tests were built and run on macOS with an XCTest stand-in: 41 tests, 0 failures.
  - The full package, all test files and the app target were typechecked for Mac Catalyst against the `vta-mobile-core-v0.6.17` headers, with no errors. `PairingScanner` was stubbed there because VisionKit is unavailable on Catalyst.
  - `xcodegen generate` plus the new ATS check were verified in both directions.
- **Still needs CI and a device:**
  - `xcodebuild test` on the simulator;
  - the app build;
  - on a device: QR pairing, the re-pair Face ID/passcode prompt, the Settings Save flow, and push wake queuing a sign-in.

title: fix: apply a network egress policy to mediator and VTA endpoints (0.8.0)
body:
## Summary

Before connecting, the SDK checked only the scheme of the endpoints a mediator's DID document advertises (REST, auth, WebSocket). It did not check the VTA REST `baseUrl` at all, and auth requests followed redirects. This PR adds a shared egress guard and applies it at each of those call sites. It is released as 0.8.0 because of the behaviour changes listed below.

Refs: SEC-4045 (F1).

## Changes

**New module: `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js/net-guard`.** It has no dependencies and runs in browsers, MV3 extensions and Node.

- `assertSafeEndpoint(url, policy)` applies these rules:
  - parses the URL with WHATWG `URL`;
  - checks the scheme (`https:`/`wss:` by default);
  - rejects userinfo;
  - refuses `localhost`, `*.localhost`, `*.local`, `*.internal` and `*.home.arpa`;
  - refuses non-public IP literals, including their IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 forms;
  - applies an optional `allowHosts` list of exact hosts or `*.` suffixes.
- `guardedFetch(fetchImpl, policy)` checks each URL, forces `redirect: "manual"`, and rejects any 3xx or `opaqueredirect` response.
- `isBlockedIp(ip)` is the shared IP classifier. It fails closed on anything it cannot parse.
- `BlockedEndpointError` has a stable `code: "E_BLOCKED_ENDPOINT"`, plus `reason`, `url`, `host` and `label`.
- The package root also exposes the module as `netGuard`, and exports `BlockedEndpointError` and `BLOCKED_ENDPOINT` by name.

**New module: `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js/net-guard/node`.**

- `guardedLookup(policy)` filters DNS answers at connect time, for use with `http(s).request`, `https.Agent` or an undici `Agent`.
- It is Node-only and not re-exported from the root, so browser bundles never import `node:dns`.

**`netPolicy: { allowInsecure, allowPrivate, allowHosts }`** is now accepted by `authenticateToMediator`, `resolveMediator`, `parseMediatorEndpoints`, `MediatorSession`, `connectVtaViaMediator`, and VTA REST `authenticate` / `refresh`.

**Mediator auth:**

- The REST and auth endpoints must pass the policy for `https:`, and the WebSocket endpoint for `wss:`.
- If any endpoint fails, the whole document is rejected.
- Requests go through `guardedFetch`, which also wraps a caller-supplied `fetch`.

**`MediatorSession`** checks `mediator.wsEndpoint` when it is constructed and again before each socket open.

**VTA REST auth** checks `baseUrl` before building any request, and uses `guardedFetch`.

**Errors:** mediator and VTA REST auth errors no longer include response bodies in the message. The body is on `err.body` and the HTTP status on `err.status`.

**Release:** version 0.8.0, a CHANGELOG entry (Security / Added / Changed / Migration), and a README section.

## Behaviour changes and migration

- `allowInsecure: true` now allows plaintext schemes only. It no longer admits loopback or private hosts.
  - For local development against `http://localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, a LAN address or a `*.local` name, use `netPolicy: { allowInsecure: true, allowPrivate: true }`.
- The top-level `allowInsecure` option on `authenticateToMediator`, `resolveMediator` and `parseMediatorEndpoints` still works, as a deprecated alias for `netPolicy.allowInsecure`. When both are set, `netPolicy` wins.
- `MediatorSession` refuses a `ws:` endpoint unless `netPolicy.allowInsecure` is set. If you construct it yourself, pass it the same `netPolicy` you give `authenticateToMediator`. `connectVtaViaMediator` forwards it for you.
- VTA REST `authenticate` / `refresh` refuse an `http:` `baseUrl` unless `netPolicy.allowInsecure` is set.
- To handle refusals, check `err.code === "E_BLOCKED_ENDPOINT"`, then `err.reason`: `invalid_url`, `scheme`, `userinfo`, `private_address`, `private_name`, `not_allowlisted` or `redirect`.
- To read the server response, use `err.body` and `err.status` instead of parsing the error message.
- A custom `fetch` must honour `redirect: "manual"`.
- In production, passing `netPolicy.allowHosts` with the expected mediator and VTA hosts is recommended. In a browser it is the only control that also covers a public name resolving to a private address.

### Consumer follow-up (pnm-browser-plugin)

- Bump `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` to `^0.8.0` once this is published.
- `packages/core/src/didcomm/index.ts`: pass `netPolicy` to `resolveMediator` and `authenticateToMediator`, and pass the same `netPolicy` to `new MediatorSession(...)`. Without that, a dev `ws://` mediator is refused when the session is constructed.
- Dev configuration: change `allowInsecure` to `{ allowInsecure: true, allowPrivate: true }`.
- Supply `allowHosts` from the configured mediator and VTA hosts where they are known.
- The generated `.d.ts` now declares `netPolicy`, `allowInsecure`, `resolve` and the full `mediator` shape, so the local re-typing of `authenticateToMediator` can go.
- Surface `E_BLOCKED_ENDPOINT` distinctly in UI and diagnostics.

## Not in this PR

- did:webvh resolution, which goes through the global `fetch` inside `didwebvh-ts`, and the inbound `resolveSender` fallback. Both are planned next, reusing `net-guard`.
- Resolver cache limits and CI action pinning.
- Blocking single-label hosts, and per-CIDR private allowances in place of the all-or-nothing `allowPrivate`. Both are open design decisions.
- Timeouts / `AbortSignal` on the auth fetches (R1.2). The gap predates this PR and is unchanged.

## Testing

- `npm test` on Node 26.7.0, with the Rust round-trip helper built: 254 tests, 254 pass, 0 fail. Without the helper: 249 tests, 242 pass, 7 skipped (the helper-dependent tests).
- The same suite on Node 20.20.2 (the CI version), with the helper: 254 pass, 0 fail.
- `npm run build:types` passes and generates `types/net-guard.d.ts` and `types/net-guard-node.d.ts`.
- `npm pack --dry-run` lists `src/net-guard.js`, `src/net-guard-node.js` and both `.d.ts` files at 0.8.0.
- Each commit passes the suite on its own: 240 after the first commit, 254 after the second.
- New test files:
  - `test/net-guard.test.js`: ip, url, names, scheme and redirect vectors; allow-list; error shape; `guardedFetch`.
  - `test/net-guard-node.test.js`: DNS answer vectors, and a real `http.get` through `guardedLookup`.
  - `test/mediator-auth-ssrf.test.js`:
    - a local `node:http` listener receives no requests for loopback / mapped-IPv6 / `localhost` endpoints, including with `allowInsecure`;
    - the positive control with `allowPrivate` receives 2 requests;
    - redirect targets receive 0 requests;
    - a caller-supplied `fetch` is never called for a refused endpoint;
    - mediator DID-document vectors;
    - `netPolicy` passthrough in `connectVtaViaMediator`.
- Added to existing test files:
  - `test/mediator-transport.test.js`: the spy `WebSocketImpl` is never constructed for a refused endpoint (e.g. `wss://10.0.0.5/ws`), and the endpoint is re-checked before dialing.

- [ ] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no new fetch call sites. Existing auth fetches still have no timeout; unchanged, see "Not in this PR".
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a.

title: Harden push endpoint validation, outbound client, and add CI
body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the gateway's outbound push path and the registration
boundary, and adds a CI workflow. It is the first round of the SEC-4045
remediation for this repository.

### Endpoint / egress policy (new `src/egress.rs`)

- An `EgressPolicy` validates a Web Push endpoint: `https` only, port absent
  or `443`, no userinfo, no fragment, IP-literal hosts refused, maximum length
  2048 bytes, and the host must match a label-boundary allow-list.
- Built-in Web Push hosts: `fcm.googleapis.com`,
  `updates.push.services.mozilla.com`, `web.push.apple.com`, and the
  label-boundary suffix `*.notify.windows.com`. Overridable via
  `GATEWAY_WEBPUSH_ALLOWED_HOSTS` (comma-separated; the `@default` token
  expands to the built-ins; wildcards at a registrable-domain level are refused
  at startup). The effective list is logged at startup.
- An `is_public_ip` classifier refuses loopback, private, carrier-grade NAT,
  link-local (cloud metadata), documentation, benchmarking, multicast and
  reserved ranges, including the IPv6 forms that embed an IPv4 destination
  (mapped, compatible, NAT64, 6to4).
- A `GuardedResolver` (a `reqwest::dns::Resolve`) fails closed when a name
  resolves to any non-public address, so there is no unchecked second lookup.

### Where it is enforced

- `handle_register` validates the registration (endpoint policy, subscription
  keys, APNs token/topic, FCM token, controller DID) and rejects without
  storing.
- `WebPushSender::send` re-validates the endpoint and keys before dialling;
  `ApnsSender::send` re-checks the token.
- `Store::open` drops stored records that fail current validation, with a
  warning.

### Outbound client (one shared constructor)

All three senders build their `reqwest` client from a single hardened
constructor: redirects disabled, proxies ignored, https only, the guarded
resolver, connect (5 s) and total (10 s) timeouts. The wake path also wraps the
send in a 15 s timeout. Loopback is permitted only under a `#[cfg(test)]`
policy.

### Request bounds

- `DefaultBodyLimit::max(16 * 1024)` on `/trust-tasks`.
- Per-field bounds on registration (endpoint length, subscription key shapes,
  APNs token hex 64–200 chars, APNs topic, FCM token charset/length, controller
  DID length/prefix) and a bound on the wake `mediator` hint.

### APNs topic policy

Registrations may name only topics in `GATEWAY_APNS_TOPICS`. When unset, a
warning is logged at startup and the check is not enforced, so existing
deployments are unaffected.

### CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D
warnings`, `cargo test`, and `cargo deny check` (only when `deny.toml` is
present). Every action is pinned to a full commit SHA with a version comment,
the workflow token is `contents: read`, and the toolchain is installed via
`rustup`.

### Docs

README updated: the "raw token never leaves the gateway" wording now reflects
that the token is sent to the platform push service and, when persistence is
enabled, written to the store file in cleartext; the new env vars are
documented; a Security-notes entry describes the egress constraints and body
limit.

## Tests

Table-driven egress tests (reject/accept vectors, the `is_public_ip` table,
host-list and topic configuration), a sender test proving a 302 is not followed
and the redirect target sees zero connections, a timeout-bound send test, an
integration test that registers the SSRF payload and is rejected with
`gateway_register_total 0`, and body-limit / field-validation integration
tests.

## Out of scope (later rounds)

TTL / caps / rate limiting (rest of PG-2), store at-rest permissions/encryption
(PG-3), the controller trust policy (PG-9), the metrics-endpoint split (PG-6),
and the allowlist bound (PG-4) are intentionally not in this PR.

title: fix(health): probe only public HTTPS transport endpoints, and never follow a redirect
body:
## Summary

`openvtc health` probes the transport URLs published in each resolved DID document. Those URLs come from documents anyone can publish, and the probe client dialled them as written: any scheme the filter let through, any host, the system proxy, and up to 10 redirects. Resolution itself was already guarded by `affinidi-did-web`, but that guard lives on the resolver's own HTTP client and never reached the probe.

The probe now applies the same policy:

- **Probe client** (`probe_client`): redirects disabled (a 3xx still counts as reachable), no proxy, a connect timeout, and, by default, `affinidi_did_web::guarded_dns_resolver()`. That resolver refuses a hostname that resolves to a non-routable address and connects only to the addresses it checked.
- **URL vetting before any I/O** (`vet_probe_url`). The DNS guard never sees IP-literal hosts, so the parsed URL is checked first. It refuses:
  - an unparseable URL;
  - a non-HTTPS scheme (plaintext endpoints are listed, not dialled);
  - userinfo;
  - a loopback, private, CGNAT, link-local or `localhost`/`.local` host, checked after WHATWG canonicalisation.

  The parsed URL that was vetted is the one sent.
- **New `Probe::Blocked { url, reason }`** (`"status": "blocked"` in `--json`, additive). `grade()` returns `None` for it. It adds a finding line, and a DNS-guard refusal found in the error chain also maps to it. `is_healthy` is unchanged: a blocked endpoint is reported, not treated as a broken chain.
- **`--allow-private-probes`** on `health` restores plaintext and private-address probing for local development stacks, and prints a one-line warning when used. Userinfo and non-HTTP schemes are still refused. `build_report` stays public-only; `build_report_with_progress` now takes a `ProbePolicy`.

The host classifier is a local copy of `affinidi-did-web` 0.1.4's (`openvtc-core/src/net_guard.rs`), with that crate's test vectors. It is marked to be replaced by the exported API once `affinidi-did-web` publishes one. `affinidi-did-web` becomes a direct dependency at the version already in `Cargo.lock`, so there is no new crate and no version change (the lockfile diff is one line).

## Breaking change (library API)

`openvtc_core::health::build_report_with_progress` gains a `policy: ProbePolicy` argument, and `Probe` gains a variant. The only in-tree caller is `openvtc/src/health_cmd.rs`, which is updated.

## Tests

New in `openvtc-core/src/health.rs`:

- `probe_refuses_loopback_literal_without_dialing`: a loopback listener sees no connection.
- `probe_refuses_plain_http`
- `probe_client_dns_guard_refuses_localhost_name`: the DNS guard is installed and its refusal is recognised in the error chain.
- `probe_does_not_follow_redirects`: the redirect target receives no request.
- `health_report_blocks_did_peer_inline_internal_service`: end to end through `build_report`, for both plaintext and HTTPS forms.
- `probe_urls_are_vetted_after_canonicalisation`: alternate IP encodings, IPv6 forms, names, userinfo, schemes.
- `allow_private_admits_dev_endpoints_but_not_credentials`
- `a_blocked_probe_is_a_finding_but_not_a_fault`: JSON shape, finding line, health unchanged.

New in `openvtc-core/src/net_guard.rs`: the classifier vectors from `affinidi-did-web`.

title: chore: remove scratch and captured-output files from the repo root
body:
## Summary

Removes eleven files at the repository root that were committed by accident, and
adds ignore rules plus a CI check so they don't come back.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `joblog.txt`, `cilog.txt` (empty) | Downloaded GitHub Actions job log |
| `full.txt`, `integ.txt`, `testout.txt`, `ws.txt` | `cargo test` output |
| `census.txt`, `census2.txt` | Trust Task census output |
| `_cap.txt`, `_rec.txt` | Rust snippets |
| `_mod.bak` | Stale copy of `vta-service/src/trust_tasks/mod.rs` |

These are the only `.txt` / `.bak` / `.log` files tracked at the root. Nothing in
the tree references them: no script, doc, test or `include_str!` / `include_bytes!`.

## Changes

- `git rm` the eleven files.
- `.gitignore`:
  - `/*.txt`: root-anchored, so `.txt` files deeper in the tree are unaffected. No
    tracked file matches it after this change.
  - `*.bak` anywhere.
  - `**.vtcbak` next to the existing `**.vtabak`, covering the default
    `cnm backup export` output name.
  - The existing `*.log` rule did not match the job log because it was saved as `.txt`.
- `ci.yml`: one extra step in the `authz-context-types` job, which already does a
  checkout and nothing else heavy. It fails if `git ls-files -- ':(glob)*.txt'
  ':(glob)*.bak' ':(glob)*.log'` returns anything. `:(glob)*` does not cross `/`, so
  only the root is checked. It is placed away from the `features` job region that
  other open PRs edit.

## Testing

- `ci.yml` parses as YAML.
- The guard step run locally:
  - On this branch: exit 0.
  - On an unmodified `origin/main` checkout: lists the eleven files, prints the
    `::error::` and exits 1.
  - On a temp index with only a nested `docs/fixture.txt`: exit 0.
- `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` prints nothing, so no tracked file becomes ignored.
- `git check-ignore`: `joblog.txt`, `x.bak`, `sub/x.bak`, `*.vtcbak` are ignored;
  `docs/a.txt` is not.

No secrets were found in the removed files, so no history rewrite is proposed.

title: ci: pass workflow inputs to run steps through env and validate them
body:
## Summary

Three `run:` scripts substituted `${{ }}` expressions straight into the script
text. This changes each one to read the value from an environment variable set in
the step's `env:`, and validates the two `workflow_dispatch` inputs before they are
used. `pr-title.yml` already uses this pattern for the PR title.

## Changes

### `join-didcomm-soak.yml`

- `inputs.runs` and `inputs.parallel` are passed as `RUNS` and `STREAMS` in the Soak
  step's `env:`.
- The script checks `RUNS` against `^[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$` and `STREAMS` against
  `^[1-9][0-9]?$`, and exits with an `::error::` otherwise.
- Both inputs are declared `type: number`, keeping the defaults of 40 and 4.
- `inputs.log` was already passed via `env: RUST_LOG` and is unchanged.

### `publish.yml` (`release-plz-release`)

- New step `Validate the recovery input`, which runs only when `package` is
  non-empty. It sits **before** `Authenticate to crates.io (Trusted Publishing)`, so
  a malformed value fails the run before a registry token is minted.
- The check is `[[ "$PACKAGE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$ ]]`. `[[ =~ ]]`
  anchors the whole value, whereas `printf | grep -E` is line-oriented and would
  accept a multi-line value whose first line matches.
- `Publish one crate` now runs `cargo publish -p "$PACKAGE"`, with `PACKAGE` in the
  step's `env:`.

### `docker.yml`

- `matrix.binary` and `matrix.tag` are passed as `BINARY` / `IMAGE` via `env:` and
  quoted. They are static matrix values, but after this no `run:` body in
  `.github/workflows/` contains a `${{ }}` expression.

A scan of every workflow found no other `inputs.*`, `github.event.*` or
`github.head_ref` inside `run:`. `ci.yml` uses `github.head_ref` only in a job-level
`if:`. The repo has no composite actions.

## Testing

- All six workflow files parse as YAML. A PyYAML walk of every `run:` body finds zero
  `${{ }}` expressions.
- Rendered the new Soak body and ran it with `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`,
  with `cargo`, `jq`, `nproc` and the test binary stubbed:

  | `RUNS` / `STREAMS` | Result |
  |---|---|
  | `40"; touch /tmp/sec4045_pwned; echo "` / `4` | `::error::runs must be an integer from 1 to 9999`, exit 1, no file created |
  | `40` / `$(touch /tmp/sec4045_pwned)` | `::error::parallel must be ...`, exit 1 |
  | `0`, empty, `40\n<cmd>` / `4` | exit 1 |
  | `40` / `4` (the defaults) | `soaking: 4 concurrent streams x 40 iterations = 160 runs` ... `no reproduction in 160 runs across 4 streams`, exit 0 |

- The validation step accepts `vta-sdk` and `vta_sdk2`. It rejects, with exit 1, a
  value containing quotes and `;`, `vta-sdk\n<cmd>`, `-Zunstable`, and a 65-character
  name.
- `Publish one crate` with a stubbed `cargo` receives a hostile value as one literal
  argument (`argv[x"; touch ...; echo "]`), and no command runs.

Not run: `actionlint` / `zizmor`, which were not available locally. A manual dispatch
of `join_didcomm soak` with the defaults after merge will confirm the `type: number`
inputs render as before.
